title: WCL Asst. Foreman (Electrical) — Mock 13
pattern: WCL Asst. Foreman (Electrical) CBT (100 Q · 100 marks · 120 min · no −ve)

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The minimum illumination level for main underground roadways in mines is:
questions.solution: Main roadways require minimum 5 lux. Working faces ≥10 lux.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A flameproof luminaire in a gassy mine must have:
options: Ex d or Ex e certification with temperature classification
questions.solution: All luminaires in gassy mines must be certified flameproof or increased safety.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A mine sub-station transformer converts:
options: HT (11 kV or 33 kV) to LT (415 V or 660 V or 1100 V)
questions.solution: Mine substations step down 11/33 kV to utilization voltages.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The typical secondary voltage of a mine distribution transformer for continuous miners is:
questions.solution: Underground mining equipment commonly operates at 660V or 1100V.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A transformer in underground mine should be of:
options: Dry-type (cast resin) or SF₆ type for fire safety
questions.solution: Underground mines prefer dry-type transformers to eliminate oil hazard.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The cooling class of a mine transformer is typically:
options: AN (Air Natural) or AF (Air Forced) for dry type
questions.solution: Dry-type mine transformers use air natural or air forced cooling.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Cable fault detection in mines is done using:
options: Cable fault locator (thumper), insulation tester, and time domain reflectometer
questions.solution: Combination of megger, TDR, and thumper is used.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A TDR (Time Domain Reflectometer) for cable fault location works by:
options: Sending a voltage pulse and measuring reflection from fault
questions.solution: TDR sends pulse and measures reflection from impedance discontinuity (fault).

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The 'thumper' method for cable fault location involves:
options: Sending high-voltage DC pulses and detecting the fault discharge sound
questions.solution: Thumper sends high-energy DC pulses causing audible discharge at fault point.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Pump station electrical in mines typically includes:
options: Pump motor, starter, protection relays, and local control panel
questions.solution: Pump stations include motor, starter, protection, and auto control.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Belt conveyor drive in mines uses:
options: VFD-controlled motor for smooth start and variable speed
questions.solution: VFD provides smooth acceleration and speed control.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The motor rating for a main belt conveyor in underground mine is typically:
questions.solution: Main belt conveyor motors range from 50–500 kW.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A belt conveyor slip detection system uses:
options: Speed sensors on drive and tail pulleys to detect slip
questions.solution: Speed sensors compare drive pulley and belt speed to detect slip.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Ventilation fan motors in mines are typically:
options: High power (50–500 kW) squirrel cage induction motors
questions.solution: Main ventilation fans require large 3-phase squirrel cage motors.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The starter for a ventilation fan motor in a gassy mine should be:
options: Flameproof or surface-mounted in safe area with remote control
questions.solution: Ventilation fan starters must be flameproof or located in safe area.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Shaft winder (hoist) electrical system uses:
options: Wound rotor induction motor or DC motor with Ward-Leonard control
questions.solution: Shaft winders use wound rotor IM or DC motors with Ward-Leonard.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The braking system for a shaft winder includes:
options: Electromagnetic (fail-safe) spring-applied brake and dynamic braking
questions.solution: Safety brakes are spring-applied and electrically/hydraulically released.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Over-speed protection for a shaft winder is achieved by:
options: Centrifugal overspeed switch that trips the drive
questions.solution: Overspeed switch (115% rated speed) automatically trips the winder.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: As per MVTR 1966, refresher vocational training must be given to persons employed in mines at least once in:
questions.solution: MVTR 1966, Rule 8: refresher training at least once in every 5 years.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A trolley wire system in mines is used for:
options: Supplying power to trolley locomotives for haulage
questions.solution: Trolley wire provides DC power to mine locomotives.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The voltage of trolley wire system in mines is typically:
questions.solution: Trolley wire systems typically operate at 120–250V DC.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The pantograph on a mine locomotive collects current from:
questions.solution: Pantograph maintains sliding contact with overhead trolley wire.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Battery charging stations for mine LHDs should be located in:
options: Well-ventilated area with gas monitoring, away from face
questions.solution: Charging areas need good ventilation, gas monitoring, and fire protection.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The battery type used in mine LHDs is typically:
questions.solution: Mine LHDs are traditionally powered by lead-acid batteries; lithium-ion is increasingly used but lead-acid remains the typical/traditional choice.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Under the Mines Rescue Rules 1985, the breathing apparatus kept at a rescue station or rescue room shall:
options: Be of the same type and make
Be of different types for flexibility
questions.solution: MRR 1985, Rule 11(4): breathing apparatus at a rescue station/room must be of the same type and make for interchangeability.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A battery charger for mine LHD should have:
options: Automatic charging profile with temperature and voltage monitoring
questions.solution: Modern chargers use CC-CV profile with temperature compensation.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: As per the Mines Rescue Rules 1985, a rescue station shall be under the charge of a Superintendent assisted by at least:
options: 2 instructors and a rescue brigade of at least 18 rescue-trained persons
questions.solution: MRR 1985: a rescue station has a Superintendent, at least 2 instructors and a rescue brigade of at least 18 rescue-trained persons.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The energy stored in a shot-firing exploder capacitor is calculated by:
questions.solution: Energy stored: E = ½CV² where C is capacitance and V is charging voltage.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: An intrinsically safe exploder for coal mines limits output energy to prevent:
questions.solution: IS exploder limits energy below minimum ignition energy of methane.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Continuous miner electrical system monitoring includes:
options: Motor temperature, insulation resistance, earth leakage, and gas detection
questions.solution: Comprehensive monitoring: temp, IR, ELR, pilot circuit, and gas detector.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The integral gas detector on a continuous miner is designed to:
options: Detect CH₄ and automatically trip power if above safe level
questions.solution: Built-in CH₄ detector trips power if methane exceeds 1%.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A shearer in longwall mining is powered through:
options: Armored festoon cable system on maingate side
questions.solution: Shearer power supplied via festoon cable system along maingate.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The festoon cable system for a shearer consists of:
options: Multi-core cable suspended from trolley wire with sliding contacts
questions.solution: Festoon system: flat multi-core cable with C-shaped current collector shoes.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Soft starter for mining equipment provides:
options: Gradual voltage ramp-up for reduced starting current and torque
questions.solution: Soft starter gradually increases voltage, reducing inrush current.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: VFD (Variable Frequency Drive) in mining applications provides:
options: Variable speed, soft start, and energy savings
questions.solution: VFD varies both frequency and voltage for precise speed control.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A VFD for a mine ventilation fan provides the benefit of:
options: Energy savings through speed reduction during low-demand periods
questions.solution: Fan power ∝ speed³. Small speed reduction gives significant energy savings.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The protection relays on a mine transformer include:
options: Overcurrent, earth fault, Buchholz, and winding temperature relays
questions.solution: Comprehensive protection: overcurrent, earth fault, Buchholz, temperature.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The function of a Buchholz relay on a mine transformer is to:
options: Detect internal faults by sensing gas from oil decomposition
questions.solution: Buchholz relay detects gas from internal faults.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A pressure relief device on a mine transformer opens to:
options: Relieve internal pressure during fault preventing tank rupture
questions.solution: PRD opens at set pressure to prevent catastrophic tank rupture.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The winding temperature indicator (WTI) on a transformer measures temperature by:
options: Simulated winding temperature using oil temperature + hot-spot model
questions.solution: WTI combines oil temperature with modeled hot-spot rise.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Remote monitoring of mine electrical systems allows:
options: Real-time monitoring of equipment status, alarms, and energy from surface control room
questions.solution: SCADA/PLC systems enable real-time monitoring from surface.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A mine power monitoring system typically monitors:
options: Voltage, current, power, PF, energy, temperature, and fault status per equipment
questions.solution: Comprehensive monitoring: V, I, kW, kVA, kVAr, PF, kWh, temperatures, faults.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Energy monitoring in mines helps to:
options: Identify waste, optimize usage, and reduce electricity cost
questions.solution: Energy monitoring identifies inefficient equipment and peak demand.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The main advantage of using 1100V supply (instead of 415V) for mining equipment is:
options: Lower current for same power, enabling smaller cables and less voltage drop
questions.solution: Higher voltage → lower current → smaller cables and less losses.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Cable reel for mining equipment is used to:
options: Store cable when not in use
Automatically pay out and retract trailing cable during tramming
questions.solution: Cable reel automatically winds/unwinds trailing cable as equipment moves.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A hydraulic pump motor on a continuous miner is typically:
questions.solution: Hydraulic pump motors range from 50–150 kW.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The electrical control panel of a continuous miner includes:
options: Contactors, overload relays, PLC/controller, gas detector interface, and displays
questions.solution: Control panel houses contactors, protections, PLC, and HMI.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The PLC (Programmable Logic Controller) in mining equipment controls:
options: Sequential operation of motors, safety interlocks, and monitoring functions
questions.solution: PLC manages start/stop sequences, interlocks, safety trips, and diagnostics.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Flash-proof barriers in mine electrical installations are used to:
options: Contain arc flash energy and prevent propagation to adjacent equipment
questions.solution: Arc flash barriers protect adjacent equipment and personnel.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The motor protection circuit breaker (MPCB) in mining equipment provides:
options: Overload, short-circuit, phase loss, and earth fault protection
questions.solution: MPCB combines overload, short-circuit, and phase-loss protection.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A phase sequence relay in mine power system protects against:
options: Incorrect phase sequence which can cause reverse rotation of motors
questions.solution: Phase sequence relay detects wrong phase rotation.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Undervoltage protection in mine motor circuits prevents:
options: Motor from restarting automatically when voltage returns after a power failure
questions.solution: Undervoltage protection prevents automatic restart after power restoration.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: As per DGMS Circular 2/2010, strata and dump slope monitoring is mandatory for dumps exceeding ______ in height.
questions.solution: DGMS Circular 2/2010: monitoring (including slope stability radar / real-time monitoring) is made mandatory for dumps exceeding 60 m height.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A shot-firer who has not been employed in blasting duties for more than 6 months shall undergo:
options: Retraining in the handling of explosives before resuming such duties
Fresh refresher training of six months
questions.solution: MVTR 1966, Rule 13: retraining in handling of explosives is required after an absence from such duties exceeding 6 months.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A person re-employed after an absence exceeding one year from mining work must undergo refresher training within:
questions.solution: MVTR 1966, Rule 10: refresher training within 1 month of re-employment after absence over 1 year.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: DGMS (Tech.) (S&T) Circular No. 02 of 2010 deals with:
options: Design, control and monitoring of pit and dump slopes in opencast mines
questions.solution: DGMS (Tech.) (S&T) Circular No. 02 dated 06.07.2010 concerns design, control and monitoring of pit and dump slopes in opencast mines.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Under the Mines Vocational Training Rules 1966, a person before being employed in a mine for the first time must undergo:
options: Informal training under any senior workman
Initial vocational training in the prescribed subjects
A medical certificate from any private practitioner
questions.solution: MVTR 1966, Rule 6: every person is given initial vocational training before first employment.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: 'Competent person' under the Mines Act 1952 means a person:
options: Appointed by the owner, agent or manager and possessing the prescribed qualifications
questions.solution: Mines Act 1952, s.2(1)(c): a competent person is one appointed by the owner, agent or manager with the prescribed qualifications for the purpose.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A first-aid room is required at a mine where the number of persons employed exceeds:
questions.solution: Mines Act 1952, s.21: a first-aid room is required where more than 150 persons are employed.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A rescue-trained person shall practise with breathing apparatus at least:
options: 8 times a year, of which 4 in mines
4 times a year, of which 2 in mines
questions.solution: MRR 1985: rescue-trained persons practise with breathing apparatus at least 8 times a year, including 4 practices in the mine.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A rescue room is required at a mine where the number of persons employed belowground exceeds 100 and:
options: The mine produces less than 100 tonnes a day
There is no rescue station within 35 km
questions.solution: MRR 1985: a rescue room is required when more than 100 persons work belowground and no rescue station is within 35 km.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Francis turbine is suitable for:
questions.solution: Francis: medium head 30-500m, most common type

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Kaplan turbine has:
questions.solution: Kaplan: adjustable runner blades for part-load efficiency

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Pelton wheel is used for:
questions.solution: Pelton: impulse turbine, high head >300m

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Cooling tower in thermal power plant removes:
options: Waste heat from condenser cooling water
questions.solution: Cooling tower: cools warm cooling water by evaporation

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: ESP (Electrostatic Precipitator) removes:
questions.solution: ESP: removes 99%+ fly ash from exhaust gas

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Boiler drum level control maintains:
questions.solution: Drum level: critical safety parameter for steam generation

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Economizer in a boiler preheats:
questions.solution: Economizer: recovers waste heat to preheat feedwater

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Air preheater in thermal plant:
options: Preheats combustion air using flue gas
questions.solution: APH: improves combustion efficiency by preheating air

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Superheater in boiler:
questions.solution: Superheater: raises steam temperature for higher efficiency

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Reheater in a power plant reheats:
options: Steam after partial expansion in HP turbine
questions.solution: Reheat: steam returned after HP stage, reheated, sent to IP/LP

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Condenser in steam power plant creates:
options: Vacuum for turbine exhaust for maximum work extraction
questions.solution: Condenser: maintains vacuum, maximizes turbine expansion ratio

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Feedwater heater is used to:
options: Preheat water before entering boiler using extraction steam
questions.solution: FWH: improves efficiency by preheating feedwater with bled steam

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Deaerator in thermal plant removes:
questions.solution: Deaerator: removes O2 and CO2 to prevent corrosion

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The Rankine cycle efficiency is improved by:
questions.solution: Higher T,P -> higher Carnot-like efficiency

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Solar PV cell efficiency is typically:
questions.solution: Commercial PV: 15-22% (mono-Si best)

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Wind turbine power is proportional to:
questions.solution: P ∝ v^3 (Betz limit 59.3%)

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Betz limit for wind turbines is:
questions.solution: Betz: max 16/27 ≈ 59.3% of kinetic energy extractable

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Diesel generator set efficiency is typically:
questions.solution: DG set: 30-45% thermal efficiency

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: PHWR nuclear reactor uses:
options: Heavy water as moderator and coolant
questions.solution: PHWR: Pressurised Heavy Water Reactor (CANDU type)

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: How many times does the 29th of a month occur in 400 years?
questions.solution: In 400 years: 97 leap years. So 29 Feb occurs 97 times. Total 29th of any month = 12×400 - 97 = 4497... Actually: 400 years have 4800 months. 97 of those are Feb in leap years. So 29th occurs 4800 - 97 = 4703... Let me recalculate. Every month has a 29th. In 400 years = 4800 months. But Feb in non-leap years only has 28 days. Non-leap Feb = 400 - 97 = 303. So 29th occurs 4800 - 303 = 4497 times.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Coal grade in India is determined by:
questions.solution: Coal grading based on GCV (kcal/kg)

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The largest coal producing subsidiary of CIL is:
questions.solution: SECL is the largest coal producer under CIL

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Opencast mining accounts for approximately what percentage of India's coal production?
questions.solution: Opencast: ~90% of India's coal production

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act was enacted in:
questions.solution: Coal nationalisation: 1973

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Singrauli region is known for:
questions.solution: Singrauli: coal mines + thermal power stations

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Coal production target for India by 2026-27 is approximately:
questions.solution: Target: ~1 billion tonnes by 2025-26

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Mine Quartering is used for:
questions.solution: Quartering: coal sampling technique for quality analysis

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Overburden in opencast mining refers to:
options: Soil and rock above coal seam
questions.solution: Overburden: material above the coal deposit

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Strip ratio is:
options: Volume of overburden to volume of coal
Weight of coal to weight of overburden
questions.solution: Strip ratio = OB volume / Coal volume

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Longwall mining method is used for:
questions.solution: Longwall: high-production underground method for thick seams

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Bord and pillar mining involves:
options: Extracting coal leaving pillars for support
questions.solution: Bord and pillar: rooms (bords) excavated, pillars left

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Coal washeries are used for:
questions.solution: Washery: removes impurities, improves coal quality

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Coal Controller's Organisation is under which ministry?
questions.solution: CCO: under Ministry of Coal

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: ECL stands for:
questions.solution: ECL = Eastern Coalfields Limited

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: SECL headquarter is at:
questions.solution: SECL HQ: Bilaspur (Chhattisgarh)

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Coal India Limited was formed in:
questions.solution: CIL formed: 1975 after nationalisation
